title: Ion traps
lead: Why an ion cannot be held by static electric fields alone, and the two traps that get round it: the Penning trap, which adds a magnetic field to charged endcaps, and the Paul trap, whose quadrupole potential oscillates at radio frequency.

footnotes.html: A Paul trap does not turn its potential: the drive reverses its sign at the radio frequency, $\alpha = -\beta = \cos \kOmegaRF \kt$ in Eq. (10.1), so the confining and repulsive directions swap every half-cycle, which is the oscillation the rest of the paragraph describes. A saddle that rotates confines by the same averaging and is the mechanical model of the trap.
